Subject: Order form: tailoring exit notice & termination-for-convenience language

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the thoughtful discussion yesterday. Per our conversation, we redlined a small amendment to the order form to clarify the Term/Auto-Renew/Termination-for-Convenience mechanics for Stratus’ pilot and production environments. The two asks from your side I captured were: (1) an extended notice window for termination-for-convenience during the first 12 months of the pilot, and (2) an opt-out path for auto-renew with a 60-day notice for production contracts.

Attached: redwood_orderform_v3.docx (word redline). Key points:
- Pilot accounts: proposed 90-day termination-for-convenience notice during first 12 months (instead of our standard 60-day).
- Production accounts: standard 60-day notice; auto-renew turns off unless explicit renewal executed.
- Data egress: if Customer terminates for convenience we commit to a 30-day export window and support export tooling.

Can you confirm whether Procurement + Legal prefer the 90 days for the pilot or want to counter with 60? If you want to loop in anyone else on the legal side please do. If you’re comfortable, we can produce a short amendment that only changes the notice window and egress obligations — that tends to speed up signature.

If helpful I’ll route this to our legal ops (Karthik + Laura) for a concise exception request and proposed wording.

Thanks,
Olga

Hi Olga —

Appreciate the quick follow-up and the redline. A couple clarifying points from Procurement/Legal:

1) Pilot scope: The pilot will include 3 test sites and a small production-like dataset. Legal prefers a longer notice during the pilot only if there is no material right to complete data export/cleanup; otherwise 60 days is fine.
2) Auto-renew: Procurement wants an explicit opt-out flow; their standard is that auto-renew only applies if both parties agree in writing 30-60 days prior to renewal.
3) Termination-for-convenience: If Redwood requires the 90-day window, we need a reciprocal right to terminate for convenience with a pro-rated refund for unused committed capacity.

I'm looping Alice from Stratus Legal — she’ll take point on language. Would you be able to share a one-page summary of the proposed amendment (just the clauses changed + rationale) so Legal can review quickly? That will help expedite the procurement review.

Thanks,
Jordan

Karthik/Laura —

Looping you in on a Stratus request. They received our v3 redline and Procurement/Legal (Jordan + Alice) pushed back on the 90-day pilot notice and asked for a reciprocal refund for unused committed capacity if they terminate for convenience.

My asks:
- Can Legal approve a one-off pilot exception to 90 days, or propose compromise language (e.g., 60 days + data escrow/export guarantees + pro-rated refund cap)?
- If we allow the exception, what guardrails do we require (e.g., limit to pilot accounts < $75k ARR, single-site pilots, 12-month cap)?

I pasted a suggested clause below for quick review — feel free to redline inline. I’m trying to keep it tight to speed signature: 

Suggested pilot clause (proposed replacement for Section 3.1 Term):
"During the Pilot Period (defined as the initial twelve (12) months following the Effective Date for Pilot Accounts), either party may terminate this Order Form for convenience upon ninety (90) days’ prior written notice. In the event Customer elects to terminate for convenience during the Pilot Period, Customer shall be entitled to export Customer Data for a period of thirty (30) days and Redwood will provide commercially reasonable assistance to facilitate export. Refunds for pre-paid, unused committed capacity will be prorated, provided, however, that refunds shall not exceed the aggregate fees paid by Customer for such Pilot Accounts."

I’ve attached the Word redline and a blank amendment template. Time is a bit sensitive — Jordan asked for a one-pager for Legal.

Thanks,
Olga

Attachment: redwood_orderform_v3.docx

Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Order form: tailoring exit notice & termination-for-convenience language

Olga —

Thanks for the context and the suggested wording. High-level legal position: we can accommodate a pilot-specific exception but recommend tightening the language and adding clear monetary and scope guardrails to limit precedent risk. Proposed edits below (summary):

1) Notice window: suggest 60 days (instead of 90) for pilots as a compromise. 90 days is acceptable only where pilot fees > $75,000 or the pilot includes production traffic.
2) Refund mechanics: allow prorated refunds for pre-paid committed capacity, capped at the total fees paid for the pilot, and exclude any refundable credits used for professional services.
3) Data egress: we’ll commit to 30 days of support for export tooling; require a written data export request and allow Redwood up to 45 days to complete complex exports.
4) Operational guardrails: limit the pilot exception to orders explicitly identified as "Pilot Account" in the order form, and expire the exception after the first 12 months.

Redline language (suggested):
"For orders identified as a \"Pilot Account\" and where the aggregate fees for such Pilot Accounts do not exceed Seventy-Five Thousand US Dollars (USD $75,000) during the Pilot Period, either party may terminate this Order Form for convenience upon sixty (60) days’ prior written notice. For Pilot Accounts where aggregate fees exceed USD $75,000 or where the Pilot includes production traffic, Customer agrees to provide ninety (90) days’ prior written notice. Refunds for pre-paid, unused committed capacity will be prorated and capped at the aggregate fees paid for such Pilot Accounts; professional service credits are excluded from refundable amounts. Customer must submit a written data export request; Redwood will provide commercially reasonable assistance and will complete data export within forty-five (45) days for complex exports."

I’ve attached a short summary spreadsheet with the refund cap examples (redline_summary.xlsx). If Sales wants to pursue 90 days broadly, we should route for Director-level approval (Ben) and document rationale.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Contracts
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
